By analyzing the interaction-driven collapse of the Dirac cone, we identify the conditions under which the system transitions from a semimetallic to a ferrimagnetic or antiferromagnetic state. Notably, we find that the presence of next-nearest-neighbor interactions can lead to a ferrimagnetic ground state, a phenomenon that has been difficult to achieve in other systems. Our results also demonstrate that the interaction-driven collapse of the Dirac cone is accompanied by a significant increase in the magnetic moment per site, which can be attributed to the formation of localized magnetic moments around the interaction-driven saddle points in the Brillouin zone.
